About this book

Craven & Quill's ghost trio spend their days doing the small, satisfying jobs that make a neighborhood feel like home: unlocking the café before sunrise, stacking books by the window, icing a fresh batch of pastries. Ghosts on the Early Shift follows them through 40 original scenes full of aprons, scarves, teacups and shop windows — plenty of everyday detail to color in, and just as much open space to make your own.

Every page is a full-page, single-sided design with a blank sheet behind it. This is a coloring book built around a cast and a place rather than a single spooky gag, so the mood stays warm and cozy from the first page to the last, whatever the season.

Because it's printed by Amazon on demand, we can't promise the paper is marker-proof. Heavy alcohol-based markers may still show through, so we recommend slipping a spare sheet of paper behind whichever page you're working on, and testing a new pen in a corner first.

Questions about this book

Is this too spooky for young readers?

It's a gentle, cozy kind of spooky — cafés and bookshops, not scares. There's nothing frightening on the page, but the theme and detail level are aimed at adults and teens rather than young children.

Will marker or gel pen bleed through?

Pages are single-sided with a blank sheet behind each design, which helps, but we can't promise zero bleed-through with heavy alcohol-based markers. Slip a spare sheet of paper behind the page you're coloring and test new pens on a corner first.

Is it the same size as the other two books?

Yes — all three Craven & Quill books are the same 8.5 × 8.5 inch square format, so they sit neatly together on a shelf.
